Importing the module that is used instead of the package root lets the bundler drop the rest of the barrel.
ncmake's lint-vue-imports workflow gates exactly this specifier for @nextcloud/vue, so this finding is that red check with a byte figure attached.

45 components of @nextcloud/vue are delivered although no file in src names them, no other dependency names them and no component named by either imports them: 110,417 B, 2.1 % of the static path of deck-main.js, next to 37 components the source names, 1 that other dependencies name and 16 those pull in.
NcRichContenteditable 13,067 B, NcDateTimePicker 7,131 B, NcEmojiPicker 7,020 B, NcBreadcrumbs 6,244 B, NcActionInput 5,985 B, NcFilePicker 5,411 B, and 39 more.
These arrive through the root import: under a barrel the whole component set is reachable, so the bundler must keep it. Per-component imports leave it free to drop what the app never names.
moment is on the static path: 591,461 B, 11.3 % of the static path of deck-main.js, in the build that carries every locale.

Whatever formats dates here, moment is the largest way to do it: it ships its locale data as one piece and tree-shakes away nothing. date-fns with the functions that are used, or luxon, is a fraction of it.

36 delivered files look like a webpack or CommonJS bundle. Their internal structure is not derivable from the artefact, so each counts as one file and the chunk figures below say nothing about what is inside them.
Every delivered file in js carries a source map, so every byte can be charged to the package and the module it came from.
